lines.text: An individual prediction of anticipated cellular network availability.
Your app receives arrays of curent predictions from the ``ServicePredictionProvider/servicePredictions`` asynchronous sequence.
Inspect the timing and impact properties of these predictions, and the associated confidence scores, to determine if your app takes action before a possible change in cellular conditions.

Returns a partial range up to, but not including, its upper bound.
Use the prefix half-open range operator (prefix `..<`) to create a
partial range of any type that conforms to the `Comparable` protocol.
This example creates a `PartialRangeUpTo<Double>` instance that includes
any value less than `5.0`.

upToFive.contains(6.28)       // false
upToFive.contains(5.0)        // false
You can use this type of partial range of a collection's indices to
represent the range from the start of the collection up to, but not
including, the partial range's upper bound.

A class that provices cellular service predictions about upcoming events and anomalies.
To receive predictions about changing cellular conditions, start by initializing and retaining an instance of this class.
Next, iterate over the ``servicePredictions`` asynchronous sequence with a `for`-`await`-`in` loop.

Each time your loop receives updated ``ServicePrediction`` instances, you can inspect their ``ServicePrediction/predictedStartTime``, ``ServicePrediction/predictedInterval``, and ``ServicePrediction/impact-swift.property`` properties to determine if your app needs to take action in advance of a potentially disruptive event.
While processing predictions from the ``servicePredictions`` sequence, gracefully handle any errors that it throws.
The ``ServicePredictionError/unsupportedDevice`` error indicates that WirelessInsights won't provide any predictions on this device.
However, other errors indicate recoverable failures, such as ``ServicePredictionError/connectionError``.
The following example shows a class that creates a
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/Swift/Task> to receive service predictions
and call a private helper method when it receives a sufficiently important prediction.
```swift
class PredictionHandler {
private let servicePredictionProvider = ServicePredictionProvider()
private let predictionHandlerTask: Task<Void, Never>
init() {
predictionHandlerTask = Task {
do {
for try await predictions in servicePredictionProvider.servicePredictions {
// Take action if any prediction in the current set
// has a sufficiently high impact and duration,
// with medium or higher confidence.
for prediction in predictions {
if prediction.confidenceScore.prediction == .high &&
prediction.impact >= .medium &&
prediction.predictedInterval > QuantizedInterval.short {
self.prepareForDisruptiveWirelessEvent()
} catch {
handlePredictionsError(error)
private func prepareForDisruptiveWirelessEvent() {
// Prepare for possible degradation of wireless connectivity
// by caching more data now, temporarily increasing
// retry count, or delaying network requests.
private func handlePredictionsError(_ error: Error) {
// If error is .connectionError, consider waiting and then retrying
// the loop over servicePredictions.
// For other errors, such as .unsupportedDevice, don't expect the
// ServicePredictionProvider to produce any predictions.
An asychronous sequence of current predictions.
To act on predictions about wireless service changes, use a `for`-`await`-`in` loop to iterate over events produced by this sequence as conditions change.
Each update provides either an array of ``ServicePrediction`` instances representing the current set of predictions or throws a ``ServicePredictionError``.
Only act on the most recent array of predictions received from the sequence.
> Note: The framework requires that your app have the `com.apple.developer.wireless-insights.service-predictions` entitlement in order to access predictions.
Creates a service prediction provider.
Retain a reference to this instance for as long as you need to receive events from the ``servicePredictions`` asychronous sequence.
